correctness.rationale: For a free action every nonempty restriction uniquely fixes its extending group element. The equality of the two partial compositions with id_S is equivalent, point by point on the partial domain T, to equal S-membership of x and gx. The 2-state matrix assigns exactly u for inclusion in S and 1+v for each T-eligible point; tracing its d-th power closes each permutation cycle. An element of order d has mN/d disjoint cycles, and subtracting N-1 empty-map copies gives the full polynomial without omitted terms. At u=v=1 eigenvalues are 3 and 1. The decreasing bases have a nonzero Vandermonde determinant and Cauchy plus strict base separation proves the asymptotic. The standalone checker compares direct composition-based rank coefficient enumerations with independently expanded cycle polynomials in ten finite actions and verifies exact rational inversion.

value.rationale: The family is natural: inverse monoids of restrictions of free permutation-group actions, including the 2022 cyclic monoids. Counting commuting pairs with exactly one idempotent is a nontrivial mixed invariant because pairwise idempotent commutation itself gives no information. The result obtains the full bivariate rank polynomial for all groups and all copy counts, not merely one small numerical slice. The reconstruction theorem characterizes exactly the finite-group datum seen by the invariant, and the asymptotic identifies the first nontrivial element-order layer. Explicit cyclic and Klein-four examples show concrete distinctions. The group-order spectrum rather than group isomorphism is the properly stated limitation.
